steps.title: Shared child groups of every contour type
notes: First border, following borders and fill contours get the same three child groups from add_contour_children: layer skip, line stipple and start point shift. The stipple is off by default (OPT_OFF); the start point shift is always there, with the mode Random as default.
The video starts with the mode set to Off to show the stacked seams, then switches to Random + previous layers.

lines: // 1 mm dashes, no overlap, closed in 2 interleaved passes.
// Option KEY (not index) of the default mode; avoid the start points
// of the last 3 layers by at least 1 mm.

steps.title: Read the settings
notes: read_contour_children reads the three groups of one contour type. The start point mode becomes one of the keys 'off', 'random', 'previous' or 'random_previous'; Compared layers and Minimum distance to previous start points become history_layers and min_distance.

lines: // No group -> no start point shift at all.
// Invalid option index -> 'random', which is also the factory default.

steps.title: A random start point, while the layer is built
notes: Every contour ring passes emit_contour. Its seed is made from layer number, island and ring, so a rebuild gives exactly the same start points.

For Random and Random + previous layers, apply_direction_and_start moves the start to a random point of the ring. The two modes with history need the layers below and are finished later, in the post-processing.

lines: let l_seed = RANDOM.make_seed(a_ctx.layer_nr, a_isl_info.islid, a_bsid * 1000 + a_ring);
// 'random_previous' gets a random start here as a first guess; the
// post-processing may move it again based on the previous layers.
// The seed is derived from layer, island and ring, so the result is
// reproducible: recalculating a layer gives the same start points.
// For closed polygons one of the existing polygon points is chosen.

steps.title: Away from the previous layers
notes: The post-processing step step_start_points_st runs single-threaded, from the lowest layer up, because each layer needs the start points chosen below it. It keeps one history per model and contour family.

START_HIST.apply takes up to 64 evenly spaced points of the ring as candidates, in ring order for Previous layers or shuffled for Random + previous layers. The first candidate at least Minimum distance away from the start points of the last Compared layers layers wins; if none is far enough, the farthest one is used. Compare Previous layers and Random + previous layers in the explainer: the first walks around the part step by step.

lines: let l_hist = START_HIST.get_history(a_store, l_model_index + '_' + l_vt.family, l_cfg.start_point.history_layers);
START_HIST.apply(l_poly, l_hist, l_cfg.start_point, RANDOM.make_seed(a_layer_nr, i, l_bsid));
// l_best_score starts below any real distance (distances are >= 0),
// so the first candidate always becomes the current best.
// Far enough away: take it and stop searching. Without history the
// score is Infinity, so the first candidate is taken.
// Index 0 is already the start point: no change needed.
// Remember the chosen point for the following layers (after commit_layer).

steps.title: Line stipple: dashes in several passes
notes: With the stipple on, emit_contour replaces the closed ring by a new hatch of dashes. The host function lineStippling cuts the ring into dashes of the dash length and spreads them over the passes: with 2 passes the laser first exposes every second dash, then the gaps, as in the animation at the end of the video.
Each dash has time to cool before its neighbour is melted, which helps thin walls and small features.

lines: l_hatch = CONTOURS.apply_stipple(a_hatch, a_cfg.stipple, l_seed, a_cfg.start_point ? a_cfg.start_point.mode : 'off');
// Last argument: maximum number of segments per result block
// Dashes are open paths. The start point history (post-processing)
// only works on closed contours and has no effect on them.
// warning_once: the hint is printed only once per script context,
// not once per contour (that would flood the log).
'Line stipple creates open paths: the start point mode "previous layers" has no effect on stippled contours.');

steps.title: Stipple and start point history do not mix
notes: Dashes are open paths. The history step only moves the start of closed contours, so with the stipple on, the modes Previous layers and Random + previous layers have no effect on that contour. apply_stipple writes a warning to the Build Style Log once. In the video this is the case after the second change: the stipple wins.
With Random dash start on, the dash pattern itself starts at a random position, so the dash ends do not line up from layer to layer either.

lines: // Only closed contours have a start point that can be moved; hatch
// lines and open paths (e.g. stippled contours) are skipped.

recipes.title: Spread the seams over more layers by default
recipes.why: A seam that comes back every fourth layer can still show; compare more layers.
recipes.result: New profiles use Random + previous layers, keep 2 mm away from the start points of the last 10 layers. Try the same values in the explainer.

recipes.title: Line stipple on for every contour type
recipes.why: Parts with many thin walls, where the borders overheat.
recipes.result: First border, following borders and fill contours start with the stipple switched on (1 mm dashes, 2 passes).

recipes.title: Longer dashes, three passes
recipes.why: Fewer dash ends (fewer start and stop marks) while each dash still cools.
recipes.result: 3 mm dashes in three passes, each 0.05 mm longer so that neighbouring dashes overlap and no gap stays unmelted.
